description: Confirmation-school boys lift the stone; lifting it means you are grown up, failing means you came to confirmation school too early.
A man could not marry until he could lift the stone off the ground.
Boys lifted the stone to count as proper bachelors.
Carrying the stone across one field strip (teg) as a test of strength.
Confirmation-school stone lifted into the arms.
Getting the stone off the ground passes the test.
Confirmation-school lads raised the stone to standing.
Lift the stone onto the shoulder and throw it backwards.
Extra stones laid on top of the lifting stone to add weight.
Väkikivi lifting as a regular Sunday pastime; stones in farmyards worn smooth by hands.
Women competed with men in stone lifting; the Jylhä women were famous for it.
Visitors rarely left Ritola before lifting the väkikivi with the master.
Men competed with the stone on holy evenings (pyhäillat).
